Each face of a regular octahedron is an.why: The regular octahedron is one of the five Platonic solids, and its standard description, in the first lines of its Wikipedia article and in every list of Platonic solids, is that it is made of eight equilateral triangles. "eight equilateral triangles" alone occurs over 500 times in Dolma.

notes: ABox revision, stored edit (very_unlikely): 'a Platonic solid composed of eight equilateral triangles' is the regular octahedron's standard description. Mathematics has no worlds and no indeterminate query (a fact about a number, a shape or a proof rests on definitions, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between), so the record has 4 determinate derived queries asking what the edit forces with the definitions held fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. The relation has_regular_face is functional (every face of a regular polyhedron is one regular polygon) and chains into has_face_shape through subclass_of. Related asks how many edges a regular octahedron has (12 before, 16 with square faces), which goes through the eight faces and the sides of each. It is stored by the counts through the co-occurrence of its two key terms (octahedron AND edges, 19518 in Dolma and 8950 in RedPajama); the phrase counts for '12 edges' alone are under 100 in RedPajama. Derived: two chain queries (quadrilateral, rectangle) and two inheritance queries, the class rules of a square passing to the faces (right angles; perimeter as an application). The right-angles query is used because a polygon-angle formula cannot answer it. Unrelated near asks the face shape of an icosahedron.
